prior_art.basis: Independent review by claude-independent-prior-art-reviewer-20261106: Generic AI job matching exists at very large scale, but nothing finds workers their next role before layoffs, so the Main KPI of 1,000,000,000 workers with career navigation in the project's sense is unmet. LinkedIn has over 1 billion members and a free AI Job Match, with an AI coach for Premium members (https://www.searchenginejournal.com/linkedin-reaches-1-billion-members-unveils-ai-job-search-tools/499939); these react to search, not to layoff risk. Layoff-risk navigators such as FutureFit AI and MyCareer Navigator are new and unmeasured at scale (https://solve.mit.edu/solutions/24008). Evidence that AI matching moves employment is weak: a Swedish public-employment RCT over 1.9 million users found a net employment effect of about 2 percent (https://conference.iza.org/EVAL_2023/rathelot_r3660.pdf). Open building blocks exist, e.g. Nesta's Mapping Career Causeways with ESCO and O*NET transition recommendations (https://github-redirect.dependabot.com/nestauk/mapping-career-causeways). Honest limit: if the KPI were read as access to any AI job matching, LinkedIn would already meet it; only pre-layoff prediction with measured placement gains is open work.
